title: Conditionals
summary: Choosing which code runs with if, else and else if, the ternary operator, and conditions that are not booleans.

misconceptions.description: Believes the code in braces runs whatever the condition says.
Believes a block, or the first value of a ternary, is used when the condition is false.
Believes the lines after an if block are skipped once the block has run.
Believes else runs after the if block as well, or that it needs no condition to be skipped.
Believes every else if is tested even after an earlier branch has run.
Believes the order of the branches does not matter, or that the last matching branch wins.
Believes a ternary gives back the true or false of its condition instead of one of its two values.
Believes a condition passes only when it is exactly the value true.
Judges the truthiness of text by what it says, so 0 looks falsy and an empty text looks like content.
Reads a variable at a different moment than the one asked about.

conceptCard.title: Choosing with if
conceptCard.body: An if statement runs a block of code only when its condition is true. The block sits inside curly braces. When the condition is false, JavaScript skips the block and carries on with the next line.

conceptCard.title: else and else if chains
conceptCard.body: else adds a block that runs when the condition is false. else if adds another test. JavaScript checks from the top and stops at the first true condition, so only one block of the chain runs.

conceptCard.title: The ternary operator
conceptCard.body: The ternary operator picks one of two values: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. It is a short form of if and else that gives back a value you can store or print.

conceptCard.title: Conditions that are not booleans
conceptCard.body: A condition can be any value. Falsy values skip the block, and the ones you will meet most are false, 0, empty text, null and undefined. Nearly every other value is truthy and runs the block. The text 0 is truthy, because it is not empty.
